description: Purposefully diverse 10-transition local audit set. It preserves the original four examples and adds two explicit multi-time-point chains plus a PA long-gap case. Selection uses target-side reports and labels, so this is not a statistically representative cohort, clinical adjudication, or a training sample.

pairs.audit_note: Reports and images show a marked interval increase in bilateral lung opacity/edema with a small effusion; support-device differences are also visible.
Reports and images show little interval change in bibasal atelectatic opacity and pleural effusions.
Reports and images show a marked interval change from no focal opacity/effusion to extensive bilateral parenchymal opacity with probable effusion.
The follow-up report explicitly states that a subtle residual pneumothorax cannot be excluded because subcutaneous emphysema limits assessment.
First transition in a four-time-point AP chain. The reports describe right pleural-drain placement, a smaller residual pneumothorax, and improving edema.
Second transition in the same AP chain. The drainage catheter is revised or replaced and the follow-up report no longer identifies an appreciable pneumothorax.
Third transition in the same AP chain. It provides a further short-interval follow-up with no appreciable pneumothorax while chronic fibrotic findings remain.
First transition in a three-time-point AP chain, with a 47-day adjacent-study gap across hospital episodes. It represents a >7d horizon and an expected no-common-admission linkage boundary.
Second transition in the same AP chain, 5.3 days later. The reports change from right lower-lobe collapse without pneumonia to new upper-lung opacity/pneumonia with increasing effusions.

A 53-day PA follow-up from the official test split. The reports change from stable postoperative/scarring findings to new mild pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions, adding long-horizon and projection diversity.
